hardware: 1x RTX 3060 12GB, 4 CPU threads, same as B06
engine: llama.cpp 74bca39 llama-bench, -fa 1 -ngl 99, pp512/tg64, 3 repeats; -ot patterns joined with ';' (repeating -ot silently kept only the first)

ncmoe18.cpu_resident: experts of layers 0-17 (37.5 % of expert bytes)

ot_down_all_plus_up_0_8.cpu_resident: down experts of all layers + up/gate experts of layers 0-8 (about 40 %)

ot_updown_0_17_gate_all.cpu_resident: up/down experts of layers 0-17 + gate experts of all layers (about 54 %)

findings: --override-tensor with the regex for layers 0-17 reproduces --n-cpu-moe 18 (51.6 vs 51.0 tok/s, within one standard deviation), so -ot is a drop-in way to place experts

tensor-type granularity (down experts only, all layers) was NOT better than layer granularity: 48.6 tok/s with ~33 % of expert bytes on the CPU vs 51.0 with 37.5 % — the layer-wise split stays the default
decode speed fell as more expert bytes moved to the CPU in the two heaviest configurations (42.3 and 37.7 tok/s at about 40 % and 54 %), against 48.6-51.6 tok/s at 33-37.5 %
caveats: decode stddev is 0.5-1.4 tok/s, so differences under ~2.5 tok/s are not conclusions
prompt-processing stddev is 10-50 % of the mean in these runs (the machine was not otherwise idle-tuned): pp512 numbers are indicative only
3 repeats, one model, one GPU, Linux; no quality comparison; KTransformers not tried
